subject: math
title: Adding and Subtracting to 100
seo_title: Grade 2 Adding and Subtracting to 100 Worksheets: Regrouping and Mental Math (Ontario)
standard_text: Use objects, diagrams, and equations to represent, describe, and solve situations involving addition and subtraction of whole numbers that add up to no more than 100
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on adding and subtracting to 100, matched to the Ontario curriculum: jumps on a number line, regrouping with base ten blocks, make a ten, estimating and checking, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Add tens to tens and ones to ones. Regroup when you need to.
key_sub: 38 + 25: jump +20 to 58, then +2 to 60 and +3 to 63. For 52 − 17 there are not enough ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 12 − 7 = 5 and 4 − 1 = 3, so 35.
body_html:
The idea: tens with tens, ones with ones

A 2-digit number has tens and ones. 45 is 4 tens and 5 ones. Add tens to tens. Add ones to ones.

Number sentenceAnswerWhat changes
45 + 3075the tens: 4 + 3 = 7
45 + 348the ones: 5 + 3 = 8
76 − 4036the tens: 7 − 4 = 3

Jump on an open number line

Start at the first number. Jump the tens. Then jump the ones. Jumping to the next ten makes it easier.

Subtract with regrouping

Sometimes there are not enough ones to take away. Regroup 1 ten as 10 ones.

Mental math: make a ten and compensate

Make a ten: fill up to the next ten first.

Compensate

What is 39 + 25?

39 is close to 40. 40 + 25 = 65. You added 1 too many, so take away 1: 65 − 1 = 64.

Answer: 64

Estimate and check

Before you add, find the closest tens. Your answer should be close to the estimate. To check a subtraction, add back what you took away.

Estimate

What is 47 + 26?

47 is close to 50. 26 is close to 30. 50 + 30 = 80. The exact answer is 73. 73 is close to 80, so it makes sense.

Answer: 73

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not regrouping: 52 − 17 = 452 − 7 cannot be done. Regroup 1 ten: 12 − 7 = 5. Answer: 35
Not regrouping: 36 + 27 = 536 + 7 = 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. Answer: 63
Adding tens to ones: 45 + 30 = 4830 is 3 tens. Add it to the tens: 75
Writing tens and ones side by side: 47 + 26 = 613Add the parts: 60 + 13 = 73

faq.q: What does Grade 2 learn about adding and subtracting in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 2 students add and subtract whole numbers that add up to no more than 100. They use objects, diagrams such as number lines and base ten blocks, and equations, and they use mental math for sums up to 50.

faq.q: What mental math strategies do Grade 2 students use?
faq.a: Common strategies are making a ten (8 + 5 = 10 + 3), using doubles (24 + 25 is 1 more than 48) and compensating (39 + 25 = 40 + 25 − 1 = 64).

faq.q: What is regrouping in Grade 2 subtraction?
faq.a: Regrouping means trading 1 ten for 10 ones when there are not enough ones. For 52 − 17, 52 becomes 4 tens and 12 ones, so the answer is 35.

faq.q: How can my child check an addition or subtraction answer?
faq.a: First estimate with the closest tens: 47 + 26 is about 50 + 30 = 80. Then check a subtraction by adding back: 64 − 27 = 37 because 37 + 27 = 64.

sets.title: Add tens and ones: jump on a number line

items.e: 30 is 3 tens. Add the tens: 4 tens + 3 tens = 7 tens. The ones stay the same. 45 + 30 = 75.

items.q: Count on by tens. What is 23 + 30?
items.e: Count on 3 tens from 23: 33, 43, 53. The ones stay the same. 23 + 30 = 53.

items.q: Count back by tens. What is 82 − 40?
items.e: Count back 4 tens from 82: 72, 62, 52, 42. The ones stay the same. 82 − 40 = 42.

items.q: What is 10 more than 57?
items.e: 10 more means 1 more ten. 5 tens become 6 tens. The ones stay the same: 67.

items.q: What is 10 less than 63?
items.e: 10 less means 1 less ten. 6 tens become 5 tens. The ones stay the same: 53.

items.q: Count on by tens. What is 18 + 40?
items.e: 40 is 4 tens. Add the tens: 1 ten + 4 tens = 5 tens. The ones stay the same. 18 + 40 = 58.

items.q: What is 13 + 50?
items.e: 50 is 5 tens. Add the tens: 1 ten + 5 tens = 6 tens. The ones stay the same. 13 + 50 = 63.

items.q: What is 62 − 50?
items.e: 50 is 5 tens. Take away the tens: 6 tens − 5 tens = 1 ten. The ones stay the same. 62 − 50 = 12.

items.q: Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 35 + 42?
Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 26 + 53?
Start at 41. Jump forward 30, then 7. Where do you land?
Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 52 + 26?
Jump back the tens, then the ones. What is 68 − 25?
Jump back the tens, then the ones. What is 79 − 46?
What is the missing jump?
items.e: From 45 to 75, the tens digit goes from 4 to 7. That is 3 tens, so the jump is +30. Check: 45 + 34 = 79.

items.q: Which number sentence does the number line show?
items.e: It starts at 29. It jumps +50 and +6. 50 + 6 = 56, so it shows 29 + 56 = 85.

items.q: Jump to the next ten. What is 38 + 25?
Jump to the next ten. What is 47 + 36?
Jump back to the ten. What is 64 − 29?
Find the missing number: 36 + ? = 76
items.e: The ones stay at 6. The tens go from 3 to 7. That is 4 tens: 40. Check: 36 + 40 = 76.

sets.title: Subtract with regrouping using base ten blocks

items.q: The blocks show 52. You need to take away 17. There are not enough ones. What do you do?
items.e: 52 has only 2 ones. You need to take away 7. Regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. Then there are 12 ones. Doing 7 − 2 instead is a common mistake.

items.q: You regroup 1 ten in 52. What does 52 look like now?
items.e: Take 1 ten from the 5 tens: 4 tens are left. The 10 ones join the 2 ones: 12 ones. So 52 = 4 tens and 12 ones. Check: 40 + 12 = 52.

items.q: 43 − 18. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 3 tens and 13 ones. 18 is crossed out. What is 43 − 18?
items.e: 43 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 3 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. 43 − 18 = 25.

items.q: 61 − 25. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 5 tens and 11 ones. 25 is crossed out. What is 61 − 25?
items.e: 61 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 11 ones. Ones: 11 − 5 = 6. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. 61 − 25 = 36.

items.q: 74 − 36. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 6 tens and 14 ones. 36 is crossed out. What is 74 − 36?
items.e: 74 has only 4 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 14 ones. Ones: 14 − 6 = 8. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. 74 − 36 = 38.

items.q: 35 − 19. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 2 tens and 15 ones. 19 is crossed out. What is 35 − 19?
items.e: 35 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 2 tens and 15 ones. Ones: 15 − 9 = 6. Tens: 2 − 1 = 1. 35 − 19 = 16.

items.q: 82 − 46. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 7 tens and 12 ones. 46 is crossed out. What is 82 − 46?
items.e: 82 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 6 = 6. Tens: 7 − 4 = 3. 82 − 46 = 36.

items.q: 53 − 8. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 4 tens and 13 ones. 8 is crossed out. What is 53 − 8?
items.e: 53 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 8 = 5. 4 tens are left. 53 − 8 = 45.

items.q: 90 − 34. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 8 tens and 10 ones. 34 is crossed out. What is 90 − 34?
items.e: 90 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 4 = 6. Tens: 8 − 3 = 5. 90 − 34 = 56.

items.q: Maya says 52 − 17 = 45. What mistake did she make?
items.e: In the ones, Maya took 2 from 7. But it must be 2 − 7, and you cannot take 7 from 2. Regroup: 12 − 7 = 5 and 4 − 1 = 3. So 52 − 17 = 35. Her mistake: she did 7 − 2.

items.q: The blocks show 64. What is 64 − 27?
items.e: 64 has only 4 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 14 ones. Ones: 14 − 7 = 7. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. 64 − 27 = 37.

items.q: What is 91 − 45?
items.e: 91 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 11 ones. Ones: 11 − 5 = 6. Tens: 8 − 4 = 4. 91 − 45 = 46.
70 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 4 = 6. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. 70 − 34 = 36.

items.q: What is 56 − 29?
items.e: 56 has only 6 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 16 ones. Ones: 16 − 9 = 7. Tens: 4 − 2 = 2. 56 − 29 = 27.
83 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 7 − 5 = 2. 83 − 57 = 26.

items.q: What is 45 − 26?
items.e: 45 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 3 tens and 15 ones. Ones: 15 − 6 = 9. Tens: 3 − 2 = 1. 45 − 26 = 19.

items.q: What is 81 − 9?
items.e: 81 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 11 ones. Ones: 11 − 9 = 2. 7 tens are left. 81 − 9 = 72.

items.q: What is 92 − 68?
items.e: 92 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 8 = 4. Tens: 8 − 6 = 2. 92 − 68 = 24.

items.q: Find the missing number: 52 − ? = 35
Which subtraction needs regrouping?
items.e: In 63 − 28, there are only 3 ones. You need to take away 8, so regroup 1 ten. In the others, the top ones digit is big enough.

sets.title: Mental math: make a ten and compensate

items.q: Fill the first ten frame to make a ten. What is 8 + 5?
items.e: 8 needs 2 more to make 10. 5 is 2 + 3. So 8 + 5 = 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Fill the first ten frame to make a ten. What is 9 + 6?
items.e: 9 needs 1 more to make 10. 6 is 1 + 5. So 9 + 6 = 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Make a ten. What is 7 + 6?
items.e: 7 needs 3 more to make 10. 6 is 3 + 3. So 7 + 6 = 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Make a ten for 8 + 5. 8 + 2 = 10. How many more do you add?
items.e: 5 is 2 + 3. You used 2 to make the ten, so add 3 more. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Which pair makes a ten?
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10. The others make 11, 11 and 9.

items.q: Make a ten. What is 38 + 5?
items.e: Make the next ten. 38 + 2 = 40. Then add the rest: 40 + 3 = 43.

items.q: Make a ten. What is 27 + 6?
items.e: Make the next ten. 27 + 3 = 30. Then add the rest: 30 + 3 = 33.

items.q: Make a ten. What is 36 + 7?
items.e: Make the next ten. 36 + 4 = 40. Then add the rest: 40 + 3 = 43.

items.q: Make a ten. What is 28 + 14?
39 is close to 40. 40 + 25 = 65. Now take away 1. What is 39 + 25?
items.e: You added 1 too many when you used 40. Take it away: 65 − 1 = 64. (65 forgets to take away 1. 66 adds 1 instead.)

items.q: Use a friendly number. What is 19 + 23?
items.e: 19 is 1 less than 20. 20 + 23 = 43. Take away 1: 42.

items.q: Use a friendly number. What is 29 + 18?
items.e: 29 is 1 less than 30. 30 + 18 = 48. Take away 1: 47.

items.q: 28 is 2 less than 30. What is 28 + 16?
items.e: 30 + 16 = 46. You added 2 too many, so take away 2: 46 − 2 = 44. (46 forgets to take away 2.)

items.q: Which is the same as 26 + 9?
items.e: 9 is 1 less than 10. Add 10, then take away 1: 26 + 10 − 1 = 35.

items.q: Add 10, then take away 1. What is 32 + 9?
items.e: 32 + 10 = 42. You added 1 too many, so take away 1: 42 − 1 = 41. (42 forgets to take away 1.)

items.q: Which is the same as 34 + 19?
items.e: 19 is 1 less than 20. Add 20, then take away 1: 34 + 20 − 1 = 53.

items.q: Take away 10, then add 1. What is 43 − 9?
items.e: 43 − 10 = 33. You took away 1 too many, so add 1: 33 + 1 = 34. (46 takes 3 from 9 instead of 9 from 3.)

items.q: Take away 20, then add 1. What is 50 − 19?
items.e: 50 − 20 = 30. You took away 1 too many, so add 1: 30 + 1 = 31. (29 takes away 1 more instead of adding it back.)

items.q: Use a double. 24 + 24 = 48. What is 24 + 25?
items.e: 25 is 1 more than 24. So 24 + 25 is 1 more than 48: 49.

items.q: Use a double. 15 + 15 = 30. What is 15 + 16?
items.e: 16 is 1 more than 15. So 15 + 16 is 1 more than 30: 31.

items.q: Which ten is 38 closest to?
items.e: 38 is between 30 and 40. It is closer to 40.

items.q: Which ten is 54 closest to?
items.e: 54 is between 50 and 60. It is closer to 50.

items.q: Which ten is 71 closest to?
items.e: 71 is between 70 and 80. It is closer to 70.

items.q: Which ten is 29 closest to?
items.e: 29 is between 20 and 30. It is closer to 30.

items.q: Which ten is 86 closest to?
items.e: 86 is between 80 and 90. It is closer to 90.

items.q: Which ten is 62 closest to?
items.e: 62 is between 60 and 70. It is closer to 60.

items.q: Estimate. 38 + 21 is about how much?
items.e: 38 is close to 40. 21 is close to 20. 40 + 20 = 60.

items.q: Estimate. 49 + 32 is about how much?
items.e: 49 is close to 50. 32 is close to 30. 50 + 30 = 80.

items.q: Estimate. 22 + 67 is about how much?
items.e: 22 is close to 20. 67 is close to 70. 20 + 70 = 90.

items.q: Estimate. 81 − 38 is about how much?
items.e: 81 is close to 80. 38 is close to 40. 80 − 40 = 40.

items.q: Estimate. 72 − 19 is about how much?
items.e: 72 is close to 70. 19 is close to 20. 70 − 20 = 50.

items.q: Estimate. 39 + 41 is about how much?
items.e: 39 is close to 40. 41 is close to 40. 40 + 40 = 80.

items.q: Estimate first: 52 − 29 is about 50 − 30 = 20. What is 52 − 29?
items.e: 52 has only 2 ones, so regroup: 4 tens and 12 ones. 12 − 9 = 3. 4 − 2 = 2. 52 − 29 = 23. 23 is close to 20, so it makes sense.

items.q: Estimate first: 28 + 43 is about 30 + 40 = 70. What is 28 + 43?
items.e: Tens: 20 + 40 = 60. Ones: 8 + 3 = 11. 60 + 11 = 71. 71 is close to 70, so it makes sense.

items.q: Estimate first. Which answer to 47 + 26 makes sense?
items.e: 47 + 26 is about 50 + 30 = 80. Only 73 is close to 80. 613 writes 6 tens and 13 ones side by side. 21 subtracts. 55 adds the tens as ones.

items.q: Liam says 63 − 28 = 45. He estimates 60 − 30 = 30. What should he think?
items.e: 45 is far from 30, so 45 is too big. Liam did 8 − 3 in the ones. Regroup: 13 − 8 = 5 and 5 − 2 = 3. 63 − 28 = 35.

items.q: 64 − 27 = 37. Which addition checks the answer?
items.e: Add the answer and the number you took away. You should get back to the start: 37 + 27 = 64.

items.q: 45 + 38 = 83. Which subtraction checks the answer?
items.e: Take one part away from the total. You should get the other part: 83 − 38 = 45.

items.q: Priya says 52 − 17 = 45. She checks: 45 + 17 = 62. Is she right?
items.e: The check must give back 52. It gives 62, so she is not right. 52 − 17 = 35.

items.q: Which addition checks 90 − 34 = 56?
items.e: Add the answer and the number you took away: 56 + 34 = 90. You get back to 90.

sets.title: Word problems: recess, the book fair and hockey cards

items.q: Liam has 34 hockey cards. He gets 25 more. How many hockey cards does he have now?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 30 + 20 = 50. Ones: 4 + 5 = 9. 50 + 9 = 59.

items.q: At recess, 27 students play soccer and 18 students play tag. How many students play?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 20 + 10 = 30. Ones: 7 + 8 = 15. 15 ones is 1 ten and 5 ones. 30 + 15 = 45.

items.q: The book fair has 63 books. The students buy 28 books. How many books are left?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 63 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. 63 − 28 = 35.

items.q: Owen has 71 hockey cards. He gives 27 cards to his brother. How many cards does he have left?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 71 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 11 ones. Ones: 11 − 7 = 4. Tens: 6 − 2 = 4. 71 − 27 = 44.

items.q: Which number sentence finds the missing part?
items.e: The whole is 63. One part is 28. Take the part away from the whole: 63 − 28 = ?. The missing part is 35.

items.q: In the Terry Fox Run, 38 Grade 2 students and 45 Grade 3 students ran. How many students ran?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Ones: 8 + 5 = 13. 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. 70 + 13 = 83.

items.q: There are 54 Canada geese on a pond. 18 geese fly away. How many geese are still on the pond?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 54 has only 4 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 14 ones. Ones: 14 − 8 = 6. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3. 54 − 18 = 36.

items.q: Maya has $20 at the book fair. She buys a book for $13. How much money does she have left?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 20 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 1 ten and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 3 = 7. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. 20 − 13 = 7.

items.q: Zoe read 52 pages. Ethan read 37 pages. How many more pages did Zoe read?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 52 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Tens: 4 − 3 = 1. 52 − 37 = 15.

items.q: Some children were skating at the rink. 14 more children came. Now there are 31. How many children were skating at first?
items.e: The whole is 31. One part is 14. Subtract. 31 has only 1 one, so regroup: 2 tens and 11 ones. 11 − 4 = 7. 2 − 1 = 1. 31 − 14 = 17. Check: 17 + 14 = 31.

items.q: There are 45 children at the rink. 18 children go home. Then 26 more children come. How many children are at the rink now?
The lost and found box has 36 mitts. Students find 29 more mitts. How many mitts are in the box now?
items.e: Find the total, so add. Tens: 30 + 20 = 50. Ones: 6 + 9 = 15. 15 ones is 1 ten and 5 ones. 50 + 15 = 65.

items.q: The class wants to sell 80 tickets for the book fair. They have sold 57 tickets. How many more do they need to sell?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 80 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 7 = 3. Tens: 7 − 5 = 2. 80 − 57 = 23.

items.q: For a recess snack, the class has 24 apples and 36 granola bars. How many snacks is that in all?
items.e: In all means add. Tens: 20 + 30 = 50. Ones: 4 + 6 = 10. 10 ones is 1 ten and 0 ones. 50 + 10 = 60.

items.q: Mateo has 48 hockey cards. Kai has 23 more cards than Mateo. How many cards does Kai have?
items.e: Kai has more, so add: 48 + 23. Tens: 40 + 20 = 60. Ones: 8 + 3 = 11. 60 + 11 = 71. (25 subtracts. 61 forgets to regroup.)

items.q: A sugar bush has 65 sap buckets. 37 buckets are full. How many buckets are not full?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 65 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 15 ones. Ones: 15 − 7 = 8. Tens: 5 − 3 = 2. 65 − 37 = 28.

items.q: Two Grade 2 classes collect cans for the food drive. One class has 63 cans. The other has 37 cans. How many cans do they have in all?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 60 + 30 = 90. Ones: 3 + 7 = 10. 10 ones is 1 ten and 0 ones. 90 + 10 = 100.

items.q: Ava has 72 stickers. She gives away 35. Which number sentence finds how many are left?
items.e: She gives some away, so take away. Start with 72 and take away 35: 72 − 35 = ?. The answer is 37.

items.q: A school bus has 72 seats. 46 students are sitting down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 72 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 6 = 6. Tens: 6 − 4 = 2. 72 − 46 = 26.

items.q: Leah read 34 pages on Saturday and 47 pages on Sunday. How many pages did she read?
items.e: Put the two days together, so add. Tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Ones: 4 + 7 = 11. 11 ones is 1 ten and 1 one. 70 + 11 = 81.
